A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same set-based training work. All 15 pages of v3 and 29 pages of v4, including figures, tables, equations, and appendices, are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v3 reports original image-classification experiments, MNIST ablations, a synthetic decision-boundary example, and measured training times in Section V and Appendix A.

after.justification: v4 retains original experimental results and adds output-enclosure measurements, Lipschitz constants, maximum verified perturbation radii, and additional ablations in Section 5 and Appendix B.

M1.justification: The center-loss/F-radius objective, zonotope propagation, gradient-set backpropagation, and parameter updates are retained. Appendix A already contained adversarially constructed zonotopic inputs and interval propagation of approximation errors; these are not new components in v4.

E1.justification: Both versions use MNIST, SVHN, CIFAR-10, TinyImageNet, and the same synthetic binary-classification example. The added diagnostics and ablations operate within this existing coverage.

E2.justification: Experimental comparisons retain TRADES, IBP, and SABR, while propagation ablations retain the proposed enclosure, Singh's enclosure, and IBP. DiffAi is added to the introductory schematic and discussion, without a reported experimental baseline evaluation.

E3.justification: Added protocols include output-size measurements on the first 1,000 MNIST test inputs, ten-iteration binary searches for verified radii, a CIFAR-10/CNN3 weighting sweep, and a CNN6 propagation ablation. Main benchmark budgets, architectures, preprocessing, and PGD settings remain as stated; changed existing scores do not establish reruns or altered settings.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 and Appendix B substantially expand the supporting analyses: enclosure size versus Lipschitz constants, maximum verified perturbation radii, weighting sensitivity on CIFAR-10, and propagation choices with CNN6. Existing input-set and propagation ablations also receive revised results. The decision-boundary example and training-time comparison were already present.

E5.justification: Both versions report accuracy means and standard deviations for the best three runs across five seeds, and minimum training times across five runs. Updated deviations and additional result entries do not establish a changed uncertainty-estimation procedure or increased run count.

E6.justification: Tables III/3 and IV/4 contain substantial replacements: FGSM-input fast-verified accuracy changes from 95.46% to 94.03%, and Set (IBP) propagation accuracy from 0.16% to 95.35%, reversing its ordering relative to Singh's enclosure. Table I/1 has smaller updates, including Set's MNIST verified accuracy of 95.86% to 95.89%. Tables 5, 8, 9, and 10 add results. These are reported result changes, not established same-setting improvements from a changed algorithm.

T1.justification: v4 adds a matrix-form verification proposition and revises definitions and complexity bounds. The new Eq. 7/Proposition 7 contains a dimensionally inconsistent matrix expression, while Definition 2 replaces v3's valid c+Gβ expression with incorrectly indexed generator rows and an incomplete coefficient domain. Most enclosure and backpropagation proofs retain their mathematical content after rearrangement and renaming.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the claims of novel gradient-set training, a tradeoff loss generalization, efficient differentiable set propagation, and competitive robustness with polynomial-time verification. Additional evidence does not redefine these central claims.

C2.justification: v4 interprets TRADES' smaller Lipschitz constant as explaining empirical robustness while its larger enclosures hinder verification. Appendix B adds a discussion balancing training time, empirical accuracy, and verified robustness. The earlier statement that IBP propagation performs poorly is removed, while the central enclosure-size interpretation remains.

D1.justification: New Appendix C supplies the existing toy example's 20 input-label pairs, five-layer architecture, optimizer, training budget, and robustness parameters. Section 5.1 newly reports approximately 30 minutes to verify 10,000 MNIST inputs. Conversely, Appendix A drops v3's explicit statement that IBP/SABR ReLU warm-up regularization was omitted; this removal does not establish that it was enabled.

R1.justification: v4 adds references on verification tools, partitioning, Lipschitz estimation, and output-set measurements, including Marabou 2.0, PyRAT, and beta-CROWN. It highlights DiffAi and explicitly acknowledges that its approximation slope matches DeepPoly's. These expand the existing positioning without replacing the central novelty argument.

P1.justification: v4 edits terminology and notation, expands introductory and verification explanations, adds acknowledgements and author affiliations, and reorganizes the appendices into A–D. The six-section main narrative and much of its prose remain. Some new explanations introduce errors, notably defining falsified accuracy as PGD attack success despite retaining a higher-is-better interpretation.

P2.justification: The entire document changes from a compact two-column layout to a single-column format, with extensively resized and relocated displays. Figure 1 gains a DiffAi panel, figure legends and labels are revised, four tables are added, and the propagation table gains maximum verified accuracies. The original training-time table is retained as Table 11.

improvement.justification: The added enclosure-size, verified-radius, and ablation evidence strengthens empirical support, while Appendix C improves reproducibility of the existing toy example. However, v4 introduces an incorrect falsified-accuracy description and malformed mathematical expressions in Definition 2 and Eq. 7/Proposition 7. These gains in evidence and losses in mathematical and explanatory clarity leave the overall quality direction uncertain.
